description: One workplace incident and the investigation of it. 29 CFR 1904 is the rule behind the recordability columns; the rest of this record exists because an investigation IS NOT A FORM SOMEBODY FILLS IN ONCE. It opens at the scene, on a phone, with whatever is known in the first ten minutes — who, what, where, who saw it, what was done immediately. Root cause arrives days later, after the witnesses have been interviewed and the machine has been looked at. Corrective actions arrive after that, and closing needs them documented and a date set to check they happened. So the status walks Open → In Progress → Corrective Actions Pending → Closed, the narrative is a table that grows, and nothing about this record assumes a single session.

fields.description: Open is the record made at the scene. In Progress means somebody is actively investigating. Corrective Actions Pending means the cause is known and the fix is not done yet — the state most investigations sit in longest, and the one a status of just Open/Closed cannot express. Closed needs corrective actions documented and a follow-up date set.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Open
In Progress
Corrective Actions Pending
Closed

fields.description: How bad it was. Drives nothing automatically — recordability is a separate determination somebody makes and states — but it is what a list of open investigations sorts on when a safety manager has twenty minutes.
fields.label: Severity
fields.options:
Near Miss
First Aid
Medical Treatment
Lost Time
Hospitalisation
Amputation
Loss of Eye
Fatality

fields.description: When it happened. Separate from when it was reported, because the gap between the two is itself a finding — and because OSHA's 8-hour fatality and 24-hour hospitalisation clocks run from this one.
fields.label: Occurred At

fields.description: Who is running the investigation. Named because an investigation with no owner is the one that is still Open in March.
fields.label: Investigation Lead

fields.description: The account of the incident. A Text and not a Small Text: 'describe what happened' is the first question an investigator asks and the last one a field should truncate. Written at the scene with whatever is known; everything learned afterwards goes in the narrative table rather than over the top of this.
fields.label: What Happened

fields.description: Which register the place is in — 'Field', 'Housing Unit', 'Asset Register'. The same dynamic pair Farm Task uses, so a task raised about the scene and this report key alike.
fields.label: Location DocType

fields.description: Where it happened, in words. Kept alongside the link because 'the third ladder from the north end of the packing line' is not a docname and is what somebody standing there needs.
fields.label: Location Description

fields.description: v0.211.0. Where the report was made, or the pin the reporter dropped: decimal degrees. Empty when the phone had no fix or the reporter declined.
fields.label: Latitude

fields.description: The fix's horizontal accuracy in metres, as the phone reported it. Empty for a pin dropped by hand.
fields.label: Location Accuracy (m)

fields.description: The machine involved, where there was one. Scanning its tag afterwards is how a worker finds out this happened here.
fields.label: Asset
Injury
fields.description: Empty on a near miss, and a near miss is worth recording precisely because it is empty — it is the same event with a better outcome.

fields.label: Injury Type
fields.options:
Laceration
Fracture
Sprain or Strain
Burn
Chemical Exposure
Heat Illness
Eye Injury
Crush
Amputation
Respiratory
Other

fields.description: What treatment was given. THE RECORDABILITY LINE RUNS THROUGH HERE: 29 CFR 1904.7 turns on medical treatment beyond first aid, and first aid is a defined list rather than a judgement — which is why this is a Select and why the determination below is stated separately by a person.
fields.label: Medical Treatment
fields.options:
None
First Aid Only
Medical Treatment Beyond First Aid
Emergency Room
Hospitalised

fields.description: What was done in the first minutes: the machine locked out, the block closed, the ambulance called. Asked for at the scene because it is the part nobody remembers accurately a week later, and because an investigation that cannot say what was done immediately cannot show the hazard was controlled.
fields.label: Immediate Actions Taken
OSHA Recordability
fields.description: 29 CFR 1904. Whether this goes on the 300 log is a determination a person makes and states the basis for — not something this app infers from a severity dropdown, because the consequence of being wrong is a citation and the reasoning is what an inspector asks to see.

Undetermined is the honest state of a report ten minutes old and is the DEFAULT deliberately: a record that defaulted to 'No' would put an unmade decision on the 300 log's right side. An investigation cannot close while this says Undetermined.
fields.label: OSHA Recordable

fields.description: WHY. 'Medical treatment beyond first aid — sutures — under 1904.7(b)(5)' is a determination an inspector can check; 'No' on its own is one they will ask about. Required by the tool whenever the answer stops being Undetermined.
fields.label: Basis for Determination

fields.description: Set where 1904.39 requires a call to OSHA — 8 hours for a fatality, 24 for an in-patient hospitalisation, amputation or loss of an eye. A flag rather than a computation, because the clock starts when the employer LEARNS of it and only a person knows when that was.
fields.label: Immediately Reportable to OSHA
Root Cause and Corrective Actions
fields.description: Filled in over days, not at the scene. An investigation that had these on the first screen would get 'operator error' written into it in the first ten minutes, which is the answer that stops anybody looking further.

Why it happened, past the immediate cause. 'The guard was removed' is a fact; 'the guard was removed in June to clear a jam and nothing put it back because no one owns the checklist for that line' is a root cause. A Text, for the same reason the incident description is one.
fields.label: Root Cause

fields.description: What is being changed so it does not happen again. REQUIRED TO CLOSE: an investigation that identified a cause and changed nothing is a filing exercise, and closing one is the moment that becomes permanent.
fields.label: Corrective Actions

fields.description: When somebody will check the corrective actions actually held. Required to close, because a fix nobody verified is a fix that gets undone the next time the line jams.
fields.label: Follow-Up Date
Investigation Narrative
fields.description: The investigation as it happened, appended and never edited. Four days of work is four or forty entries, each stamped when it was written and attributed to whoever wrote it — which is the whole reason a hearing believes any of it.

name: Accident Report
